scenes.narration: In 1876, chunks of meat apparently started falling from a clear Kentucky sky.
On March 3rd, a woman named Mrs. Crouch was outside her home in Bath County when pieces of flesh suddenly began dropping around her.
The shower reportedly lasted several minutes.
And this wasn't just a few tiny scraps.
Contemporary accounts described pieces scattered across the ground, with some reportedly several inches long.
There was no obvious animal overhead.
And witnesses were left with a deeply strange question: What exactly had just fallen from the sky?
Samples were examined, but reports disagreed over what kind of tissue it actually was.
Some observers even tasted the mysterious meat.
But one explanation eventually became much less supernatural.
Vultures sometimes defend themselves—or lighten their load for flight—by vomiting partially digested food.
If a flock had been passing overhead, several birds regurgitating at once could have created what looked like a bizarre meat shower.
That explanation was proposed for the Kentucky incident, although the exact circumstances were never definitively established.
So Kentucky probably didn't experience meat magically materializing in the clouds.
But in 1876, people really did report pieces of flesh raining onto a farm—
and more than a century later, the Kentucky Meat Shower remains one of America's strangest historical mysteries.
